case_title: Naresh Kumar v. State of Haryana
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304-B (dowry death); Evidence Act s.113B presumption discussed
evidence_type: Testimonial evidence of relatives on dowry demands; suicide note (Exhibit P-4); medical evidence; investigation evidence; statutory presumption under s.113B Evidence Act
aggravating_circumstances: Death within 10 months of marriage after repeated dowry demands, threat of divorce, and death by burn injuries
trial_court_outcome: Convicted appellant and co-accused; sentence not stated in this judgment
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction of appellant upheld; co-accused mother and brother acquitted
neutral_facts: The victim was married to the accused in July 2000. After the marriage the victim was allegedly harassed for insufficient dowry, and the accused raised a demand for a motorcycle, in addition to demands made by the accused's mother and younger brother. About three months after the marriage the victim telephoned her father about the demands. The victim's father and uncle met the accused and his relatives and asked that the victim not be harassed, but the harassment continued. In April 2001 the victim again complained by telephone. The uncle brought the victim to her parental home, but the next day the accused came, insisted that the victim be sent back, and threatened divorce; the victim was sent with the accused. On 1 May 2001 the victim's family received word that the victim had suffered burn injuries and had been taken to hospital. There, the victim told the victim's father, uncle and brother-in-law that the victim had been beaten and set on fire by the accused and the accused's family members. The victim died of extensive burn injuries. The victim's father lodged the first information report, and an investigating officer conducted the investigation and sent the accused for trial. The prosecution relied on testimony of relatives about dowry demands, medical evidence and investigation evidence. A suicide note stated that nobody should be held responsible and that all doors were closed for the victim. The defence contended that the victim had taken her own life because of pressure from an uncle over parental property, and that relations with the accused were cordial.
physical_harm: Death of victim from extensive burn injuries
motive: Demand for dowry (motorcycle and further dowry) from the victim's family
key_evidence_accepted: Consistent testimony of victim's father, uncle and brother-in-law on dowry harassment soon before death; medical evidence of death by burning; suicide note read in context; s.113B presumption
witness_credibility: Three prosecution witnesses (victim's father, uncle and brother-in-law) found to have specifically and categorically deposed about dowry demands soon before death; their evidence accepted
trial_duration: offence: 1 May 2001 (death from burn injuries); trial judgment: not given; High Court: 12 March 2013; Supreme Court: 14 November 2014
legal_representation: Appellant: G.C. Shahpuri, Surinder Singh, Balbir Singh Gupta; Respondents (State of Haryana and others): Kamal Mohan Gupta
investigation_status: FIR lodged by victim's father (Exhibit PA/1); investigation completed by SI and accused sent up for trial
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted appellant and co-accused. High Court: conviction of appellant upheld, co-accused acquitted. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence upheld
defence_argument: Demand of dowry not proved soon before death; suicide note stated nobody should be held responsible and contained no dowry allegation; parity with acquitted mother and brother
legal_principle_applied: Dowry death requires harassment soon before death; suicide note does not exonerate husband; husband's responsibility is higher than other relatives; statutory presumption under s.113B and failure to explain as additional circumstance
precedent_relied_upon: Hira Lal and Ors. v. State (Govt. of NCT) Delhi, 2003 (1) Suppl. SCR 734: (2003) 8 SCC 80 (relied on); Manohar Lal v. State of Haryana, AIR 2014 SC 2555 (referred to and distinguished)
sentencing_rationale: Not stated; concurrent conviction and sentence upheld as no reason to interfere was found
judicial_aggravating_factors: Death within 10 months of marriage following dowry harassment; no separate sentencing aggravation identified by the court
other_sentence_order: Appellant directed to surrender to undergo remaining sentence, failing which he may be arrested and committed to custody
